summary.text: Eunice Lehmacher is a retired medical social worker and psychotherapist from Clemson and the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 3rd District. She has worked as a counselor, teacher, librarian and church educator, serves on two local bodies, and previously ran unsuccessfully for the South Carolina House in 2020 and 2024. According to her Ballotpedia survey, her campaign emphasizes health care access, energy costs and affordability.

paragraphs.text: Born in Lexington, Missouri, and grew up in Wilson, North Carolina, and Knoxville, Tennessee.

Earned a high school diploma from South Young High School, a bachelor's degree from Concordia University (1985), and a master's degree from the Catholic University of America in Washington, D.C. (1996).
Her career includes work as a high school math and science teacher, library associate and church educator, according to Ballotpedia.
Moved to Clemson, South Carolina, with her husband in 2002, where they raised two sons, according to her Ballotpedia survey.

Worked as a medical social worker and psychotherapist for Oconee Memorial Hospital, Clemson University, Hospice of the Foothills and other health care agencies, and owned a private counseling practice in Seneca, SC.
Was the Democratic nominee for South Carolina House of Representatives District 3 in 2020 and 2024, losing the general election to Jerry Carter (R) in 2020 and to Phillip Bowers (R) in 2024.
Serves by gubernatorial appointment on the Anderson Oconee Pickens Mental Health Commission and on the Sustainability Advisory Committee for the City of Clemson.

Describes volunteer work teaching classes, leading support groups, mentoring students and leading community groups including the Sierra Club and her neighborhood association; has been affiliated with the South Carolina Society for Clinical Social Workers and the Clinical Social Work Association.
Won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary with 53.4 percent of the vote over Ernest Mackins.
